# Tariff Manufacturing Checklist For Moving To The United States

Time to read 5 min

With rising tariffs on imported goods, many businesses are considering relocating their manufacturing operations to the United States.

  

Transitioning production domestically can help mitigate tariff-related costs, improve supply chain efficiency, and enhance product quality. [...] Once your location and partners are in place, it’s time to re-evaluate your supply chain.

  

Identify domestic sources for your key raw materials. For packaging, that includes corrugated board, paperboard, adhesive, inks, and more. Local sourcing can reduce lead times, minimize risks from global disruptions, and make just-in-time manufacturing more viable. [...] Supply chain disruption is another common pain point. Transitioning from overseas suppliers to domestic ones takes time. Establishing redundancy in your supply chain—multiple sources for the same raw material—can mitigate risks. For packaging, where timing is everything, any delay can derail a launch or retail reset.
